question: Drug the choice for hyperthyroidism in first trimester of pregnancy is
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Hyperthyroidism treatment in pregnancy" -> "Safety for fetal development is crucial" -> "Propylthiouracil is preferred in the first trimester" -> "Lower risk of teratogenic effects" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Hyperthyroidism management options" -> "Methimazole is effective" -> "Higher risk of congenital malformations" -> "Not preferred in first trimester" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Carbimazole is a pro-drug of Methimazole" -> "Similar risks as Methimazole" -> "Not recommended in first trimester" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Perchlorate is not commonly used" -> "Limited data on safety in pregnancy" -> "Not a first-line treatment" -> 70%
analysis: In the first trimester of pregnancy, Propylthiouracil (PTU) is the preferred treatment for hyperthyroidism due to its lower risk of teratogenic effects compared to Methimazole. Methimazole is generally avoided in the first trimester because it has been associated with congenital malformations. Carbimazole is a prodrug of Methimazole and carries similar risks. Perchlorate is not commonly used due to safety concerns. Therefore, the best choice is Propylthiouracil.
